subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when no explicit binding matches, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The current source behavior and security concern are clear, but fallback semantics affect session state, provider/model choice, permission boundaries, and existing multi-account upgrades, so automation should not choose the permanent routing contract.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings only
options.body: Leave runtime routing unchanged and add clearer docs, doctor, or status warnings for Discord accounts that appear intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair or replace the fork PR
options.body: Use the linked fork PR as source material only after conflicts, phantom-agent guards, distinct match diagnostics, and real Discord proof are addressed.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for multi-agent routing, multi-account providers, and recent routing policy work.
